package_info.package_manager: N/A (CI/CD platforms, not traditional package managers)
package_info.package_versions: Jenkins: versions vulnerable to CVE-2024-23897; TeamCity: versions vulnerable to CVE-2023-42793
package_info.why_malicious: These CI/CD platforms, when unpatched, contain vulnerabilities that allow remote code execution (RCE). Attackers exploiting these flaws can gain unauthorized access to build servers, manipulate build processes, steal sensitive assets (source code, signing certificates), and inject malicious code into software supply chains, impacting downstream consumers.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (remote code execution via web interface or API)
execution_context.file_location: Jenkins core server (exploited via HTTP API endpoints)

malicious_snippets.code_language: shell (executed via Java Runtime from Groovy/Java context)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker exploits a Jenkins RCE vulnerability to execute arbitrary shell commands, downloads a remote payload, and executes it on the build server, enabling full compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution via web/API interface is highly abnormal and dangerous, especially when used to download and run external scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Jenkins operation should not allow unauthenticated or unauthorized users to execute arbitrary code on the server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Jenkins admins may run scripts for maintenance, but never via untrusted or unauthenticated sources.
key_indicators: Use of Runtime.exec or similar APIs in web-exposed endpoints
Network calls to external, non-whitelisted domains
Execution of shell commands from CI/CD server context

execution_context.file_location: Injected into build scripts or server configuration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial compromise, the code reads sensitive Jenkins secrets and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltration of secret keys and credentials is a clear sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build scripts should never access or transmit server secrets to external locations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use case for exfiltrating master.key outside the organization.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files (e.g., master.key, credentials.xml)
Outbound network requests to untrusted domains
Use of command-line tools for data exfiltration

execution_context.file_location: Injected into build pipeline scripts (e.g., build.gradle, pom.xml, build steps)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During the build process, the code uploads built artifacts to an external server, enabling attackers to tamper with or analyze the software before public release.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized transfer of build artifacts to external locations is a hallmark of supply chain compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build artifacts should only be published to trusted, internal repositories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Artifact uploads to internal artifact repositories (e.g., Nexus, Artifactory) are legitimate.
key_indicators: Build scripts containing external upload commands
Network destinations outside approved artifact repositories

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits Jenkins/TeamCity RCE vulnerability to gain code execution on the CI/CD server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Privilege escalation and persistence on the build server

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses and exfiltrates sensitive secrets and credentials from the compromised server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to impersonate build server or access downstream systems

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects malicious code or exfiltration steps into the build pipeline, targeting downstream consumers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Supply chain compromise and potential distribution of trojanized software

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected execution of shell commands via CI/CD web/API interfaces
Outbound network connections to untrusted or unknown domains from build servers
Access to sensitive files (e.g., secrets, credentials) by build scripts
Modification of build pipeline scripts to include external uploads
file_indicators: Build scripts (Jenkinsfile, build.gradle, pom.xml, etc.) containing curl/wget or external upload commands
Unexpected changes to /var/lib/jenkins/secrets/* or TeamCity configuration files
Presence of unauthorized scripts or binaries in build workspace
network_indicators: HTTP/S POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker.com, webhook.site)
Unusual artifact uploads to non-corporate endpoints
Outbound connections during build or post-build steps
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD server logs for unexpected script execution, especially via web/API endpoints. Alert on build scripts or pipeline definitions containing network upload commands to non-approved domains. Track access to sensitive files and outbound network activity from build environments. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes to build scripts and configuration files.
